sources.title: Evidence for a Regulatory Role of Diatom Silicon Transporters in Cellular Silicon Responses
sources.publication: Shrestha and Hildebrand, Eukaryotic Cell 14:29-40, January 2015; prepublication 7 November 2014
sources.acquisition: Full PMC HTML, methods/results/discussion/captions and Figures 7-8 pixels inspected. Supplement acquisition blocked through checked PMC, EuropePMC and publisher routes.
sources.claim: Conditional joint SIT1/SIT2 perturbation affects net Si(OH)4 depletion and PDMPO silica incorporation in CCMP1335.
locators: Results: Effect of SIT downregulation on Si transport and incorporation
limits: 20 micromolar and 200 micromolar assays have different outcomes; Figure 8C is incorporation not a direct uptake assay despite discussion wording.
Knockdown, not deletion; joint targets, all-SIT antiserum, no main-text rescue.
Colorimetric net depletion and PDMPO fluorescence are distinct proxies; neither establishes isolated product mass or elemental silicon.
n=3 SD stated, biological versus technical unspecified.
Main methods 24 h starvation versus caption overnight; retain both.
No main-text measured pH or abiotic depletion blank.
Sensing is a hypothesis, upstream sensor alternative remains.

sources.title: Microbes a Tool for the Remediation of Organotin Pollution Determined by Static Headspace Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
sources.acquisition: Full EuropePMC XML and successful alternative PMC HTML inspected; Figures 3-4 pixels inspected via NCBI CDN. XML reports no supplement; supplementary API timeout preserved, not treated as proof of absence.
sources.claim: C22-inoculated prepared sediment exhibits TBT decrease and DBT/MBT signals consistent with debutylation.
limits: C22 source sequence is generically bacterium; paper Enterobacteriales genus wording does not resolve taxon.
Nominal 100 ng/g tributyltin chloride; analytical results reported ng/g wet sediment, not proven elemental Sn basis.

TBT final 52.73 ng/g exceeds the highest stated linear calibration limit of 50 ng/g (§2.3.1). Section 2.3.2 separately reports sediment spike-recovery accuracy over 5-60 ng/g wet weight (n=3), 94-103% recovery, RSD below 10% across tested organotins. Dilution or linear-calibration extension above 50 ng/g is not described; recovery tests do not reach the nominal 100 ng/g starting spike. Analytical recovery is not microbial extraction yield; exact TBT percentages remain quantitatively uncertain.
5 g per replicate to 15 g total appears pooled; n=3 repeated assays do not establish independent biological means.
No matched sterile-broth or killed-cell arm described; no cell counts/sterility follow-up.
C22 MBT declines between 90 and 120 d; downstream products and total-Sn balance unmeasured.
Certified-reference validation proposed, not performed; analytical spike recovery is not biological recovery.
Figure 4 ethylated formulas reflect analytical derivatization, not environmental metabolites.
No toxicity endpoint, purified product, tin oxidation-state assay or industrial deployment.

candidate_handoff.title: Bioleaching of indium and tin from used LCD panels
candidate_handoff.status: Known round6 lead; full 7-page publisher PDF text inspected via web, local downloads403. Figures not visually assessed. Deferred separate mechanism.
candidate_handoff.findings: Willner et al. 2018, PPMP 54:639-645. Adapted acidophile mixture, 2.5% w/v LCD feed at 30 C, initial pH 1.9, 9K/S0 versus acid/S0, sterile controls. Tin extraction exceeds 90% in both 9K biotic and control; final Table 2 tin 3.15 versus 4.59 mg/dm3. No blanket microbial advantage. Reprecipitation/phase explanations speculative, biological series replication unclear.
candidate_handoff.next_action: Acquire local PDF and visually assess Figures 2/4, verify acidophile identity and chemistry; curate narrow comparative leaching context if needed. Existing indium record not edited.
